newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones slashes profit outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones slashes profit outlook.

text.p: Department store group David Jones Ltd said on Friday it had lowered its first half net profit forecast by up to 50 percent due to lower revenues and higher depreciation charges.

"Continuing depressed retail trading conditions in the key Christmas trading months of November and December have reduced sales and earnings of the David Jones Ltd department store group," the company said in a statement.
The company said as a consequence it had lowered its earnings forecast for the 26 weeks ending January 25, 1997 by up to 50 percent.
David Jones chief executive Chris Tideman said the bulk of the expected decline was due to reduced gross profit and significantly higher depreciation charges.
Tideman said the recent reductions in Australian interest rates were too late to have any meaningful impact on Christmas trading.
"Hopefully, the lower rates will have a positive effect on consumer confidence and spending as they feed through into disposable income in 1997," he said.
David Jones reported a net profit of A$44.64 million for the six months to January 27, 1996 on sales of A$790.31 million.
In November last year the company said its first quarter sales fell 2.9 percent from a year earlier to A$310.5 million.

David Jones said for the first five months of the 1996/97 financial year, sales in its stores were 0.7 percent below the corresponding months of 1995/96 and sales at its John Martin's stores in South Australia were down 21.8 percent.
The company said the sharp reduction in gross profit stemmed from an adverse product mix.

The group said it experienced poor sales of apparel, shoes and accessories, which historically accounted for nearly 50 percent of David Jones's total sales and traditionally provided retailers with their highest profit margins.
"While there was some improvement in sales of electricals, cosmetics and food, these products failed to counter the drop-off in sales of higher margin products," Tideman said.
Tideman said increased depreciation charges were due to new stores and the extensive upgrading of systems within the David Jones group.
Tideman said the lacklustre retail trading environment experienced throughout 1996 had continued during November and December.

"Despite good trading in the Christmas week, which included the start of clearance sales for the David Jones Group, those two months were also 2.9 percent below the same period of the previous year," the company said.
David Jones shares closed nine cents weaker at A$1.67.
